Seminar Title:

Design and Development of a Twin-Screw Extruder with Machine Learning-Based Process Control and Quality Prediction for High-Moisture Meat Analogues

Abstract:

High-moisture meat analogues (HMMA) are textured protein products developed from plant-based proteins such as pea, soy and wheat proteins to mimic the texture and structure of animal meat. High-moisture extrusion (HME) involves simultaneous heating, mixing, shearing, conveying and cooling. The screw configuration, moisture content, temperature, screw speed and cooling-die conditions strongly influence protein transformation and the development of fibrous, anisotropic structures. Although several studies have investigated the effects of formulation and operating conditions on HMMA quality, the integrated effects of extruder design, multiphysics material behaviour, predictive modelling and dynamic process control remain comparatively less explored. Multiphysics modelling can provide insights into material flow, heat transfer and deformation, thereby supporting rational design of the extrusion system. The proposed research aims to develop an Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered indigenous laboratory-scale smart twin-screw extruder (TSE) for HMMA production. The work will involve the design and fabrication of the feeder, screw elements, barrel, cooling die, sensing and control systems, followed by structural, thermal and multiphysics simulations to assess component integrity and material behaviour. The fabricated TSE will subsequently be commissioned and experimentally validated. Experimental studies will be conducted to investigate the effects of formulation and critical process parameters on HMMA quality attributes, including texture, structure, and colour. The resulting experimental dataset will be used to develop forward machine-learning models for quality prediction and inverse models for determining suitable process conditions. These models will further support dynamic adjustment of critical TSE parameters for targeted HMMA quality. Finally, the developed HMMA will undergo cooking and storage studies under refrigerated and accelerated conditions to evaluate product stability and shelf life. The proposed framework integrates extruder design, multiphysics simulation, experimentation, machine learning and intelligent process control, providing a digital and data-driven approach for efficient development and optimization of HMMA production.
